statement: Let $A\subseteq \mathbb{F}_p$. Let\[A\hat{+}A = \{ a+b : a\neq b \in A\}.\]Is it true that\[\lvert A\hat{+}A\rvert \geq \min(2\lvert A\rvert-3,p)?\]
status: PROVED (LEAN) — erdosproblems.com: 'This has been solved in the affirmative and the proof verified in Lean.'
notes: RESOLVED IN THE AFFIRMATIVE (the Erdős–Heilbronn inequality): for every prime p and every subset A of the field F_p = Z/pZ, the restricted sumset A +̂ A = {a + b : a, b ∈ A, a ≠ b} satisfies |A +̂ A| ≥ min(2|A| − 3, p). Formalize the affirmative assertion, quantified over all primes p and all subsets A of Z/pZ; any faithful encoding of the restricted sumset is acceptable (e.g. the set of sums over pairs of distinct elements of A). The minimum is taken in the integers, so for |A| ≤ 1 the bound is negative and holds trivially. From the site: A question of Erdős and Heilbronn. Solved in the affirmative by da Silva and Hamidoune [dSHa94]. In [Er65b] Erdős mentions the more general conjecture that the number of x in F_p which are the sum of at most r many distinct elements of A is at least min(r|A| − r^2 + 1, p). This is discussed in problem C15 of Guy's collection [Gu04].
